 Bayern Munich and 1. FC Magdeburg meet in the round of 32 of the DFB-Pokal 2026/27. The match takes place this Wednesday 28 October at 19:45 (UK time) at the Allianz Arena in Munich.
 Assistant coach Aaron Danks continues in the Bayern dugout with Vincent Kompany recovering in hospital, leading a side that returned to the top of the Bundesliga with Sunday’s 3-1 win at Freiburg. Newly crowned 2026 Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane leads the Bavarian attack, which has racked up 30 goals in its last eight matches across all competitions. Standing in their path are 2. Bundesliga promotion chasers Magdeburg, who arrive in Bavaria after thrashing Karlsruher SC 6-1 on Saturday. While Petrik Sander’s side have historically troubled Bayern in this competition—famously eliminating them on penalties in 2000—their recent travel record shows three away games without a win.
 Our prediction for Bayern Munich vs. Magdeburg backs a rotated Bayern lineup to control the tie and secure a comfortable passage to the round of 16. Find out our betting tips and analysis for this cup tie.

 Bayern Munich vs. FC Magdeburg - Head-to-head record
 Bayern Munich and 1. FC Magdeburg have met three times in competitive fixtures, with Bayern winning two alongside one draw.
 Their most famous encounter came in the second round of the 2000/01 DFB-Pokal, when fourth-tier Magdeburg stunned the eventual European champions 4-2 on penalties after a 1-1 draw at the Ernst-Grube-Stadion .
 The teams have crossed paths just once in Munich, resulting in a routine Bayern victory. With Magdeburg possessing the division’s fifth-best attack in the second tier and Bayern rotating key starters ahead of the weekend Klassiker against Dortmund, Wednesday’s tie brings an engaging clash of tiers to the Allianz Arena.

 Bayern Munich - In impressive goalscoring form
 Bayern enter Wednesday’s cup fixture on a high after Harry Kane was awarded the 2026 Ballon d’Or in London on Monday night, having struck 73 goals in 65 appearances across all competitions last season. Below is an overview of the hosts’ current form, squad rotation, and projected starting XI:
 Recent form
 The Bavarians lead the Bundesliga on goal difference after Sunday’s 3-1 victory at Freiburg, extending an impressive run that has produced 16 goals across their last five matches .
 While defensive clean sheets have been hard to come by—conceding nine times in their last five fixtures—Bayern’s home form remains formidable: Danks’ side have won four of their five competitive matches at the Allianz Arena this season, scoring 18 goals in the process.
 Danks must navigate several injury absences while keeping one eye on Saturday’s league trip to Borussia Dortmund. Captain Manuel Neuer is sidelined with a foot problem, leaving Jonas Urbig to start in goal. In defense, center-back Kim Min-jae is out with a groin strain, meaning Jonathan Tah partners Dayot Upamecano (or Tarek Buchmann), flanked by Josip Stanišić and Sacha Boey (or Konrad Laimer).
 Midfield resources are stretched with Aleksandar Pavlović (calf), Bara Sapoko Ndiaye (appendicitis), and Jamal Musiala (thigh) all ruled out. Tom Bischof steps into central midfield alongside Joshua Kimmich (or Ismael Saibari).
 In attack, winger Luis Díaz is sidelined until late November with a hamstring tear, opening the door for 18-year-old Lennart Karl to start on the right wing opposite Serge Gnabry, with newly crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane leading the line.

 FC Magdeburg - In strong goalscoring form
 Petrik Sander’s side travel to Munich sitting fifth in the 2. Bundesliga on 16 points, just two points behind second-placed Nürnberg. Here is an examination of the visitors’ tactical setup, attacking firepower, and expected starting lineup ahead of kickoff:
 Recent form
 Magdeburg demonstrated their attacking potential on Saturday by thrashing Karlsruher SC 6-1, scoring four times in the second half.
 While home displays have been clinical, their form on the road has been far less dependable: Sander’s men have failed to win any of their last three away league matches , suffering back-to-back defeats at Dynamo Dresden (2-0) and Hertha BSC (2-1).
 In the DFB-Pokal, however, Magdeburg advanced comfortably with a 4-0 away win over Bahlinger SC in the first round.
 Sander has the luxury of a fully fit squad ahead of the trip to Munich. Dominik Reimann starts in goal behind central defenders Tobias Müller and Anselmo García MacNulty, flanked by full-backs Pierre Nadjombe and Alexander Nollenberger.
 In midfield, Bayern loanee Felipe Chávez screens the back four alongside Luka-Mikael Hyryläinen and Torben Müsel.
 In attack, Polish striker Mateusz Żukowski—who has five league goals and two cup strikes —leads the line, supported on the wings by top scorer Emmanuel Iyoha (six goals) and primary creator Barış Atik, who has provided five assists this season.

 Predictions for Bayern Munich vs. FC Magdeburg - Dominant home win
 Bayern Munich have scored at least three goals in six of their last eight competitive matches. Facing a Magdeburg defense that concedes chances away from home, the hosts should look to set a high tempo early on. Backing Over 1.5 goals in the first half represents a steady, high-probability opening angle.
 While Magdeburg have scored freely in the second tier, their away form has faltered against organised opposition. With Harry Kane leading the line and fresh from his Ballon d’Or triumph, Bayern have too much quality in the final third for a lower-league backline to contain. With Bayern expected to control territory and possession, backing the hosts on the -3.5 Asian Handicap line covers a comfortable three-goal margin of victory.
